Title: Speech on the occasion of the official ceremony celebrating the 30th anniversary of the Central Bank
text: Speech by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros on the occasion of the official ceremony celebrating the 30th anniversary of the Central Bank of the Comoros -Your Excellency the President of the Union of the Comoros, -Your Excellency the President of the Constitutional Court, -Your Excellency the President of the National Assembly, -Excellencies Vice-Presidents of the Union of the Comoros, -Dear Governors of the Islands, -Honourable Ministers, -Ambassador de France, representing the French Minister for Cooperation -Members of the diplomatic corps, -Honourable Members, -Dear colleagues, Governors of the partner central banks, -Ladies and Gentlemen Directors of the Central Bank, -Ladies and Gentlemen Directors General, -Ladies and gentlemen -Dear Guest, It is a great honor and pleasure for me to address such an eminent audience, as part of the celebration of the 30th anniversary of the Central Bank of the Comoros. Allow me first of all, on behalf of the Central Bank of the Comoros, to express to His Excellency Dr. IKILILOU DHOININE, President of the Union of the Comoros, to his Government and the Comorian people, our most sincere thanks for the confidence and support they bring to the Central Bank in the exercise of its missions. I would also like to express my sincere thanks to you all for honouring this commemoration with your presence and thus demonstrating your attachment to our institution. I would like to welcome to our country, to all the delegations of the partner institutions, who have made the trip to share with us this historic moment. I particularly greet the Banque de France, the Bank of Central African States, the Central Bank of West African States, the Bank of Mauritius, the Central Bank of Madagascar, the Institut d'Emission d'Outre-mer, the Directorate General of the French Treasury, the French Development Agency and the Directorate of Global Economy and Development Strategies of the French Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs. Your presence among us testifies to the spirit of openness, exchange of experiences and cooperation that drives us all. We have chosen for this celebration the theme of "monetary cooperation between the Comoros and France", which the BCC is responsible for its implementation. This cooperation is exercised in an economic and monetary area, the Franc Zone, consisting of: -the France, -eight States of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU), whose issuing institution is the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO), -six States of the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC), whose issuing institution is the Bank of Central African States (BEAC); -and the Union of the Comoros, whose issuing institution is the Central Bank of the Comoros (BCC). The basis for this cooperation is based on: -the unlimited guarantee given by the French Treasury, reflected in the unlimited convertibility of the currency issued by the Central Bank of the Comoros, -the fixed parity between the Comorian Franc (and the CFA franc) and the Euro without limitation of amount, -the free transferability of funds within the Franc Zone, -the centralization of the BCC's foreign exchange reserves with the French Treasury (at least 65% of the reserves). These assets benefit from an exchange rate guarantee vis-a-vis the SDR, the operating procedures of which are defined in the operating account agreements. Honourable Assistance, ladies and gentlemen, The history of the Central Bank of the Comoros has evolved in parallel with that of the Colonial Administration and the Franc Zone, formalized in 1939. From the 1950s, a period during which the Comoros, under French dependency, were administratively attached to Madagascar, the Bank of Madagascar and the Comoros was responsible for issuing banknotes with legal tender in Madagascar and the Comoros. On the eve of the independence of the Comoros, the Comoros Issuing Institute, created in 1974, took over the monetary issue until July 1, 1981, date of creation of the Central Bank of the Comoros. This anniversary dedicates thirty years of work during which we have built at the service of the nation, a credible Central Bank, both at the national level. than international, as a regulator of the major balances and the banking system of our country. A central bank that has been able to adapt to changes in its environment. Its statutes were renovated and modernized in December 2010, to consolidate its independence, improve its governance, strengthen its control system and its transparency. Four fundamental tasks are conferred on the Central Bank: -It guarantees the stability of the currency, defines and implements the monetary policy of the Union of the Comoros. To carry out this task, it has been able to establish a credible monetary policy, in line with its international commitments, particularly those undertaken in the context of monetary cooperation. -The Central Bank has the exclusive privilege of issuing monetary signs, notes and metallic coins. In 2005, it issued a new range of modern banknotes, reflecting its desire to provide the population with a quality cash circulation, with a reinforced level of security, in accordance with international requirements and standards. The 1000 FC note was awarded the 2006 Ticket of the Year Award by the International Bank Note Society (IBNS). In this regard, I would like to pay tribute to the quality of the work carried out by the Banknote Production Directorate of the BDF and the Monnaie de Paris. -The BCC ensures the proper functioning and security of payment and settlement systems. It has set up a clearing house for securities (cheques, transfers) in which all banks have participated since 2006, -The Bank ensures the proper functioning of the banking system. It has strengthened its system for monitoring and controlling banking and financial activities. With the support of the IMF and the BDF, it has undertaken important institutional reforms to modernise the Banking Law, strengthen prudential regulation, consolidate its supervisory mission, with a view to maintaining a healthy, profitable, liquid and solvent banking sector. I take this opportunity to commend the efforts made by the Ministry of Finance, the United Nations system and all the technical partners who have set up the Support Program for Inclusive Finance in the Comoros, whose master plan for financial inclusion in our country was recently validated by the Authorities and the Central Bank. This program supports the BCC to support its efforts and interventions in the supervision of DFIs (Decentralized Financial Institutions). Honourable Assistance, ladies and gentlemen, Since 2004 and with the will of the Government Authorities and the Central Bank, the Comorian banking and financial landscape has undergone unprecedented changes, marked in particular by the entry of new players. -The number of authorized banking and financial institutions has increased from 3 to 9. -The Ya Komor Savings and Credit Mutuals and the Anjouan SANDUK benefited the approval of the Central Bank in 2005 and 2006, -Two new generalist banks were also authorized in 2007 and 2009. -Two companies specialising in money transfers have been approved by the BCC in 2006 and 2009. -In 2005, the newly created SNPSF, inheriting the activities of the Caisse Nationale d'Epargne, set up the CCP, while developing foreign exchange and money transfer activities. In this competitive environment, -the rate of banking has improved significantly and reached 18% in 2010, -between 2005 and 2010, the volume of savings mobilized increased from 27 to 53 billion FC and credit to the private sector from 15 to 42 billion FC. -the ability of our economy to pay has benefited from this opening of the banking sector to competition, reaching a historic peak of 76 billion FC in September 2011 against 37 billion FC in 2005. This extraordinary expansion of the Comorian banking sector reflects an irreplaceable wealth of confidence that must be protected and strengthened. I would like to stress that the stability of the banking sector also depends on the legal protection of banking institutions and the establishment of an effective mechanism against financial crime. In this regard, I welcome the initiative of President IKILILOU to set up a body in charge of fighting corruption, one of the underlying crimes punishable by the anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism system. In addition to all these advances, the tasks facing the Central Bank are heavy, but exhilarating and there is no shortage of projects. They are oriented towards three axes: -Continuing the effort to modernize and strengthen the legal and regulatory framework, inspired by international best practices, -Continuing to strengthen the supervision and control of banks and financial institutions, in particular to ensure the protection of savers, -The development of cooperation with various foreign Central Banks in order to encourage the sharing of experiences and information in the field of banking supervision and regulation. In this regard, I welcome the signing in September 2011 of an agreement with the French Prudential Control Authority and an agreement with the Central Bank of Tanzania in 2009. In addition, the Central Bank has launched a project to create a central payment risks and incidents that benefits from the Fund of Expertise and Capacity Building (FERC) granted to the Union of the Comoros by the France. This project has three major objectives: -Create an environment conducive to better financing of the national economy and thus allow banks to distribute more credit, with better risk management; -Provide banks and financial institutions with reliable information on the overall debt of customers; -Give the Central Bank visibility on the quality of the credit portfolio of the banking system. Our current reflections focus on the following axes: -The strengthening of the protection of depts by the establishment of a solidarity mechanism, -The establishment of new mechanisms for indirect financing of the State, like those initiated by the other central banks of the Franc Zone. -The sharing of skills to strengthen the capacities of the Comorian financial administration and those of banks. -Support for the development of innovative products for the financing of investments. -The creation of a mechanism to support diaspora efforts, the aim of which is to continue to facilitate remittances and develop incentives for productive investment. It seems important to me to highlight the growing interest of the financial resources of the diaspora, which constitute an important lever of the Comorian economy and banking sector. The figures published by the Bank from 2005 to 2010 show an exponential growth of these resources to reach more than 250 billion FC. Every year, funds from the diaspora represent 25% of the national wealth. Migrant remittances have become increasingly important in the debates and actions of the international community. The work carried out within the G8 and the ZOF testifies to the importance of this subject, which must also be a fundamental subject in our country. The Co-development initiative is exemplary in this respect, and I welcome the recent signing of a new agreement on this plan between the Comoros and France. Honourable Assistance, ladies and gentlemen, The question that everyone can ask themselves today: has the BCC deserved the trust placed in it by the country after thirty years of existence? The results achieved, particularly in terms of national and international credibility, monetary stability, as well as the extraordinary expansion of the Comorian banking sector, reflect this well-deserved confidence. This result is also one of the commitment, dedication, involvement and expertise of the Bank's Board of Directors, government and staff. I cannot conclude my statement without paying tribute to our predecessors, both Executive Directors and Governors and former staff of the Bank. They have bequeathed us a great institution that has managed, during these thirty years, to assume with quality its major missions and its international commitments. Thank you.

Title: Reducing the costs of money transfers by migrants and optimizing their impact on development, Financial tools and products for the Maghreb and the Franc Zone
text: Restitution workshop of the study "Reducing the costs of migrants' remittances and optimizing their impact on development, Financial tools and products for the Maghreb and the Franc Zone" carried out by the association Epargne Sans Frontieres, with the support of the France through the French Development Agency, and the African Development Bank. ADDRESS BY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BCC Hotel Crystal Itsandra Moroni, January 31, 2013 Excellencies,Ladies and Gentlemen Ministers Your Excellency Ambassador of France to the Union of the Comoros, Your Excellency the Resident Representative of the United Nations System, MadamelaRepresentantedelaBanqueafricainededeveloppement Distinguished Representatives of the International Financial Institutions Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen of the French Development Agency Ladies and Gentlemen Directors General of the BEF, Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen Restitution workshop of the study, "Reducing the costs of migrants' remittances and optimizing their impact on development" carried out by the Association Epargne sans frontieres with the support of France through AFD and the AfDB. On behalf of the Central Bank of the Comoros, I would like to express our sincere thanks to the France, AFD, AfDB and the Association Epargne sans Frontiere for having kindly selected the Comoros among the countries that served as a reference framework for the work of this study. The Central Bank also welcomes the fruitful exchanges it had with the experts of the Association Epargne sans Frontieres and I take this opportunity to reiterate our thanks and congratulations for the quality of the work done. Ladies and Gentlemen, The choice to retain the Comoros among the countries that served as a reference framework was surely guided by the exceptional nature of the weight of remittances from the Comorian diaspora and their impact on the macroeconomic dimensions of our country.  26% of GDP,  179% of the State Budget,  72% of the money supply,  100% of the net foreign assets of the banking system,  662% of Foreign Direct Investment  And 356% of project donations received in favor of the Comoros. For the year 2012, the amount of transfers channeled by the banking system is estimated at more than 46 billion FC after 45.6 billion FC in 2011. These statistics illustrate the importance of this topic for our countries and in particular for the Central Bank because these funds constitute An important lever of the Comorian economy and banking sector. They are the largest source of external financing, far ahead of Official Development Assistance. MesdamesetMessieurs, At a time when the global economy is being hit by an unprecedented crisis, the theme of this workshop acquires particular resonance, especially for fragile economies. Indeed, this crisis has strongly impacted external financing flows: -Foreign direct investment, which had experienced extraordinary growth since the early 1990s, is in sharp decline -official development assistance, which was already in a major recession (excluding the HIPC initiative), has fallen considerably, On the other hand, remittances from migrants, despite economic difficulties in host countries, have been maintained or even increased. many studies carried out on this subject, in particular those conducted by the AfDB in collaboration with the Bank of France, the work carried out in the framework of the Co-development and the exchanges that took place in 2008 and 2011 at the level of the meetings of the Franc Zone. The need to reduce transfer costs is also in line with the recommendations of the G8 to halve the cost of transfers by 2014 and those of the G20, for the promotion of financial inclusion. Ladies and Gentlemen, It seems important to me to highlight, in addition to the growing interest of the financial resources of the diaspora, the actions carried out by the Central Bank in this area to facilitate the remittances of migrants and improve their impact on the economic development of our country. These include:  The opening of the banking sector to competition and the integration of microfinance networks,  The approval of new companies specializing in money transfers and foreign exchange transactions,  Approvals given to credit institutions wishing to work with international companies specializing in money transfers,  And authorizations given to local banks for the signing of partnership agreements with French credit institutions. These various initiatives have made it possible to cover a large part of the territory, to maintain at a high level the amounts transferred and above all to reduce considerably from 85% to 58% from 2001 to 2012, the amount of transfers through the informal channel. MesdamesetMessieurs, In our country, these important resources are rarely invested in income-generating activities. They are oriented in particular to consumption, expenditure on health and education, real estate investments and expenditure on major weddings. This observation shows that there is a real problem within our economy of matching the financial sphere, which is largely in surplus, and the real sphere, which needs new instruments for sustained economic recovery. The major challenge is to be able to transform these highly liquid resources into stable savings, which can finance part of the investment needs. Remittances from the Comorian diaspora in France are part of our current reflections within the Central Bank. This study, carried out by the Association Epargne Sans Frontiere and the recommendations made, will naturally contribute to deepening these reflections on the best ways to reduce the costs of transfers and optimize their contribution to economic development through financial and regulatory innovations in our country. Thank you.

Indeed, this crisis has strongly impacted external financing flows: -Foreign direct investment, which had experienced extraordinary growth since the early 1990s, is in sharp decline -official development assistance, which was already in a major recession (excluding the HIPC initiative), has fallen considerably, On the other hand, remittances from migrants, despite economic difficulties in host countries, have been maintained or even increased. many studies carried out on this subject, in particular those conducted by the AfDB in collaboration with the Bank of France, the work carried out in the framework of the Co-development and the exchanges that took place in 2008 and 2011 at the level of the meetings of the Franc Zone. The need to reduce transfer costs is also in line with the recommendations of the G8 to halve the cost of transfers by 2014 and those of the G20, for the promotion of financial inclusion. Ladies and Gentlemen, It seems important to me to highlight, in addition to the growing interest of the financial resources of the diaspora, the actions carried out by the Central Bank in this area to facilitate the remittances of migrants and improve their impact on the economic development of our country. These include:  The opening of the banking sector to competition and the integration of microfinance networks,  The approval of new companies specializing in money transfers and foreign exchange transactions,  Approvals given to credit institutions wishing to work with international companies specializing in money transfers,  And authorizations given to local banks for the signing of partnership agreements with French credit institutions. These various initiatives have made it possible to cover a large part of the territory, to maintain at a high level the amounts transferred and above all to reduce considerably from 85% to 58% from 2001 to 2012, the amount of transfers through the informal channel. MesdamesetMessieurs, In our country, these important resources are rarely invested in income-generating activities. They are oriented in particular to consumption, expenditure on health and education, real estate investments and expenditure on major weddings. This observation shows that there is a real problem within our economy of matching the financial sphere, which is largely in surplus, and the real sphere, which needs new instruments for sustained economic recovery. The major challenge is to be able to transform these highly liquid resources into stable savings, which can finance part of the investment needs. Remittances from the Comorian diaspora in France are part of our current reflections within the Central Bank. This study, carried out by the Association Epargne Sans Frontire and the recommendations made, will naturally contribute to deepening these reflections on the best ways to reduce the costs of transfers and optimize their contribution to economic development through financial and regulatory innovations in our country. Thank you.

Title: Speech at the seminar on banknote authentication
text: SEMINAR ON TICKET AUTHENTICATION Address by the Deputy Governor of the BCC Wednesday, November 27 Htel Le Moroni ******  Mr. Technical Sales Manager of the Banque de France  Madam Director of the Fund and Banking Operations of the Central Bank of the Comoros  Representatives of banks and financial institutions  Representatives of the public administrations present here  Ladies and gentlemen It is with great pleasure that we welcome Mr. Eric PEZIN technical sales manager of the bank of France to support us in this seminar dedicated to training on the authentication of Euro banknotes and Comorian Franc. Dear participants, allow me, on behalf of the Governor of the BCC and on my own behalf, to express our gratitude and sincere thanks for the interest you have given to this seminar which will be held here in two and a half days. As you know, last year, the Central Bank of the Comoros celebrated its thirtieth anniversary of its creation. Indeed, succeeding the issuing institute of the Comoros in July 1981, the Central Bank of the Comoros strives to play its role and assume the missions assigned to it by the various texts in force namelyits own statutes, Law 80-08 on the currency and the rle of the BCC in the control of banks and financial institutions, Law 80-07, known as the banking law and so on.  It has also been able to establish a credible monetary policy in line with its international commitments, particularly those entered into in the context of the monetary cooperation established in 1979 with the France. In an economy heavily dominated by cash, the security of this means of payment is paramount. During the last decade, the Central Bank has renewed its range of banknotes by issuing modern banknotes, by their design and practical by their dimensions. This renewal, benefiting from the new manufacturing technology of the Bank of France, reflects the Bank's desire to fight against counterfeiting and to offer the population quality banknotes, in terms of durability and especially security. It should be noted that the 1000 FC note was awarded the 2006 banknote of the year award by the IBNS Institute (International Bank Note Society). This seminar is part of the training of trainer actions for banking and public administration professionals in the authentication of euro and Comorian franc notes. During this seminar, you will learn about the appropriate tools and authentic characteristics to better arm yourself against counterfeiters. Thus, you will then ensure the relay for the training of the staff of sorting rooms, exchange offices and cash registers of your establishments. Ladies and gentlemen The fight against the counterfeiting of banknotes is a permanent fight that calls for constant vigilance, in order to protect our institutions and preserve the stability of the Comorian banking and financial sector. I take this opportunity to salute the efforts made by the Banks and Financial Institutions who regularly declare apocryphal notes to us. I strongly invite the Ministry of Justice to accompany us in this regard, in order to secure our currency. In closing, I would like to express my sincere thanks to the Banque de France in particular to the manufacturing department for its support in this process. I also thank Mr. Eric PEZIN, for his expertise and his great contribution to this seminar. Thank you. I declare the Seminar open

Title: Speech at the opening ceremony of the microfinance week in Comoros
text: Ministers, Distinguished representatives of the Governorate of Ngazidja Island, Distinguished representatives of development partners, Chief of Staff of the National Army, Director of AFD Dear Directors, Distinguished guests in your ranks and capacities, Ladies and gentlemen, It is a real pleasure for me to speak at this opening ceremony of the Microfinance Day in the Comoros, a day that has now entered our agendas every year. Allow me to welcome this initiative and thank the organizers of this event for their interest in the Central Bank, giving us this opportunity to briefly recall the major stages of evolution of the Decentralized Financial Institutions (DFIs), their prospects for integrated development in the banking landscape and to highlight some priority areas for the Central Bank. Ladies and Gentlemen, The first initiatives that marked the launch of new microcredit structures in the Comoros and which would later constitute the first strategy for financing basic economic initiatives and poverty reduction in rural areas, date back to the 1990s. The 1st initiative was taken in 1993 by the Comorian Government, with the support of the French Development Agency (AFD), to support the creation of Sanduk funds in rural areas and which at the time aimed to finance agricultural projects. In 1995, two years later, a second initiative was taken. The State, supported by the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), has set up the Support for Basic Economic Initiatives (AIEB) project, with a component intended for the creation of Savings and Credit Mutuals in regional capitals. During this period, bank financing of the economy was provided by only two banks, with an average outstanding credit of CF 15 billion per year. This outstanding amount now exceeds 50 billion FC At the same time, the SANDUK banks and the Mutuelles d'Epargne et de Credit have seen their activity develop rapidly, outside the scope of intervention and control of the Central Bank. In this context, under the initiative of the Central Bank and the contribution of the various partners, a Presidential Decree was signed in 2004 regulating the activities of Decentralized Financial Institutions and placing them under the authority of the Central Bank, which allowed the Sanduk and Meck networks to subsequently benefit from the approval of the BCC. This text projected a new vision of decentralized financing, first by the name of Decentralized Financial Institution and not microfinance institution and then by its flexibility that favored their integration into the national banking sector. Let me cite as an example:  The authorization given by the BCC to these new institutions to carry out foreign exchange and money transfer operations; The opportunities offered to carry out, via the Central Bank, the international operations of their client;  The development of a necessary synergy between banks and DFIs, in individual within the framework of a single Professional Association bringing together all authorised credit institutions,  The establishment of a single monetary policy, supervisory and prudential regulation framework;  The integration of DFIs into the clearing house and their participation in The future central for payment risks and incidents, which we count set up soon.  Finally, the introduction of a favourable tax system that has helped to strengthen their solvency. This strategy, which is unique in Africa, has made it possible to establish the place of DFIs in the banking and financial landscape of our country. Ladies and Gentlemen The approval of new credit institutions and financial intermediaries from 2007 has not slowed down the development of the Meck and Sanduk networks, on the contrary, they have managed to integrate into this competitive environment and consolidate their position. DFIs now have 58 funds, more than 150,000 accounts, a balance sheet size of CF 30 billion, they have FC 26 billion in outstanding savings, FC 15 billion in outstanding loans and occupy 30% of the market share of the banking sector. In 2012, they generated a consolidated profit of FC 952 million. These data illustrate the important position occupied by the Meck and Sanduk networks in the financial inclusion and banking of the population. Admittedly, these are comfortable and encouraging results, but this development cannot continue, without risk management, the establishment of an effective internal control system, and a professionalization of the sector. This is the logic advocated by the new Banking Act, which offers DFIs who have acquired the necessary skills, experience and maturity the opportunity to evolve into a mutual bank. Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, The Comorian banking and financial landscape is experiencing exceptional growth, fundamental reforms are being undertaken by the Central Bank with a view to strengthening its solidity and establishing a framework for the development of financial services. In parallel with this momentum, new needs arise to support and accompany this growth. Indeed, on the initiative of the Central Bank, with the support of AFD, a Banking and Financial Sector Development Fund has just been created, with a view to mobilizing the State, credit institutions and development partners to further support this growth and consolidate bank financing of the Comorian economy. The priority areas selected for the assistance of this fund are in particular: -The establishment of a central payment risks and incidents; -The development of electronic banking and technological innovations for financial use; -The channeling of migrant remittances through the creation of innovative products; -The establishment of a bank chart of accounts; -Strengthening banking and financial inclusion; -Capacity building of professionals in the sector and the regulatory authority. -The improvement of the clearing system and the modernization of the payment system. This fund has received financial support from the French Treasury in the amount of one million euros, a large part of which is intended to finance the establishment of the central payment risks and incidents. I take this opportunity to renew my thanks to the Comorian State, the French Treasury and AFD for this important support that gives a strong impetus to this great initiative. In conclusion, I would like to recall that our reflections on the development of microfinance must integrate the two dimensions that partly constitute its raison d'etre, in particular, its contribution to poverty reduction and access to financial services for vulnerable populations, including people living in rural areas. Finally, I would like to emphasize that, with regard to the political and strategic choices made, the Central Bank will continue to encourage and support the necessary synergy between banks and DFIs and to support the development of partnerships with foreign credit institutions, with a view to promoting bi-banking and facilitating financial transfers from the diaspora. Thank you and declare open the week of microfinance

Title: Speech at the official launch ceremony of the new 250FC coin
text: Speech of the Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros on the occasion of the official launching ceremony of the new 250 FC People's Palace coin, 02 January 2014 -Your Excellency the President of the Union of the Comoros, -Mr. Vice-Presidents, -Mr. President of the National Assembly, -Mr. President of the Constitutional Court, -Mr. President of the Supreme Court -Mr. Governor of the Island of Ngazidja, -Ladies and Gentlemen Members of the Government, -Dear Deputies, -Dear Former Presidents of the Union of the Comoros -Ambassador of France, President of the Union of the Comoros -Ladies and Gentlemen Members of the Diplomatic Corps, -Ladies and Gentlemen Directors of the Central Bank, -Ladies and Gentlemen Directors General, Honourable guests, ladies and gentlemen, It is a great honour and pleasure for me, in my capacity as Governor of the BCC, to express my warmest thanks to His Excellency Dr. Ikililou Dhoinine, President of the Union of the Comoros, for having kindly marked, despite a very busy agenda at the beginning of this year, this historic moment, by officially launching the new 250 FC coin, which will undoubtedly mark the cash circulation of our country for a very long time. Mr. President of the Republic, Your presence among us this morning is a great honor that you do to our central bank and testifies to your attachment to this great institution of the Republic; Thank you for that. At the beginning of 2014, I would like to take this opportunity to wish you health and happiness for you and your family; and also wish great success to your actions in favour of progress, peace, security and development of our country. Distinguished guests, I would also like to extend to all of you my most respectful greetings and my most sincere thanks for having kindly honoured this ceremony with your presence and once again to demonstrate your attachment to your Central Bank. Mr. President of the Republic, On December 31st, for the 1st time in the history of the Central Bank, at our invitation, you kindly agreed to visit our headquarters, exchange with the young executives who make up its lifeblood, enter our strong rooms, and appreciate our organization and our IT and security system. In the guest book, set up on this occasion, you wrote, and I quote, "a real pleasure, followed by great satisfaction, after this much desired visit, which I have just made to the headquarters of the BCC, this prestigious institution, guarantor of the good monetary governance of our country. I welcome once again the efforts made recently by the Central Bank, including the licensing of new banks, the modernization of the Banking Law and the effective implementation of the anti-money laundering and anti-terrorist financing regime." This excerpt illustrates a mark of confidence and further consolidates our reform and innovation actions, oriented on three axes: -Promote the harmonious development of the banking and financial sector, -Provide economic sectors with the means to mobilize the necessary resources to finance their needs, -Sustainably support the Comorian economy towards the path of development Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen; The Central Bank is a Comorian public institution to which the legislator has entrusted four fundamental missions: -Guarantee the stability of the currency and define and implement the monetary policy of the Union of the Comoros; -Ensure the supervision and control of banking, financial and insurance activities; -Ensure the proper functioning and security of payment and settlement systems; -Ensure exclusively the issuance of notes and coins having legal tender and discharging power in our country. This privilege is also a great responsibility that imposes on us the duty to offer our country, a quality and highly secure cash circulation. In this context, we have invested in recent years more than 3 billion FC to make available to the population, monetary signs at the forefront of technological innovations, in order to achieve this objective of quality and safety. The issuance of this new 250 FC coin testifies to this desire and marks a historic moment for our issuing institute because it devotes a long design work and a significant financial investment for the production of 8 million pieces for the entire range. I am convinced that this 250FC coin, which marks the 30th anniversary of the Central Bank and monetary cooperation with the France, as well as the other coins that are put into circulation from this morning, will provide a lasting response to the growing need for small currencies expressed by the population. I would like to thank and congratulate the Monnaie de Paris for the quality and success of the manufacture of this new coin, the success of which is already predictable. I also thank the public forces, the Chief of Staff, the Commander of the Gendarmerie and the teams made available to us to ensure the security arrangements that were necessary for its launch. I would also like to thank the ORTC and the print media for the excellent communication that followed our information campaign, which removed any confusion between divisional currency and inflation. Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, Our banking and financial sector is indeed booming, and in this momentum, with the support of the Government Authorities and our partners, we have taken the step together of opening it up to competition. Several direct and indirect jobs have been created, new financial services are offered, the rate of banking has risen sharply and in 2013, banks financed the private sector to the tune of 50 billion FC on average against 18 billion FC 5 years ago. This is a satisfactory result and a great step forward for our country. I would like to thank the political authorities that have succeeded one another over the last 10 years, for this impetus and this determination which has enabled us to go beyond the stage of the de facto monople of a single generalist bank. I would also like to thank the banks that have accompanied this dynamic to increase bank financing to the private sector. Ladies and gentlemen We have now entered the phase of consolidation of achievements marked in particular by: -the modernisation of the legal and regulatory framework governing the sector, -the strengthening of banking supervision, with a view to guaranteeing its stability, -the provision of a Central Risk and Payment Incidents, with a view to giving them the means to contain risks, identify defaulters and also give the Central Bank visibility on the overall quality of the credit portfolio. To financially support this reform momentum, a Banking Sector Development Fund (FDSB) was created by decree of the VP in charge of Finance. This fund has already received financial support from the French Treasury through budget support amounting to 1 million, part of which is already intended to finance the establishment of the risk centre. I reiterate my thanks to the Comorian Government, the French Treasury and AFD for this important support, which gives a strong impetus to this initiative. Honorable assistance The next phase will focus on: -The improvement of customer information, -The adoption in 2014 of a new text regulating the systems and means of Payment, credit cards and electronic money. The Head of State agreed to validate this text by a presidential decree in the same way as the exchange regulations. This draft text, currently under consideration by our Board of Directors, will also reduce the use of cash, pave the way for the traceability of settlement operations and contribute to the fight against corruption. Finally, I would like to stress that the stability of the banking sector also depends on the legal protection of banking and financial institutions, including the establishment of an adequate legal and regulatory framework to reduce credit risk. I hope that the text proposal made by the Central Bank on this subject will receive substantial support. I am convinced that these major achievements will contribute to improving the business climate and fostering economic development in our country. Thank you and wish you a very happy new year.

Title: Address on the occasion of the presentation of the Officer of the National Order of Merit insignia
text: Ceremony of presentation of the Insignia of Officer of the National Order of Merit to the Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros, Mr. Mze Abdou Mohamed Chanfiou by SEM. Philippe LACOSTE, Ambassador of France to the Union of the Comoros. Address by the Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros Voidjou, 18 February 2014 -Excellencies Vice-Presidents, -Your Excellency the Ambassador of France to the Union of the Comoros and Mrs. Philippe LACOSTE -Your Excellency the former President and Mrs. Azali Assoumani -Your Excellency the President of the National Assembly, -Your Excellency the Director of Cabinet of the President of the Republic -Mr President of the Constitutional Court, -Honourable Ministers, -His Eminence the Great Mufty, -The Governor of Ngazidja Island, -Members of the diplomatic corps, -Mr. Chief of Staff of the DNA, -Mons dear father Mohamed Ben Charaf, -The North-East Prefect -Mr. Chairman of the Board of Directors of the BCC -Distinguished Executive Directors of the Central Bank, -Former Governors of the BCC -Mr. Deputy Governor, -Ladies and Gentlemen Directors General, -Distinguished guests, -Dear collaborators, -Ladies and gentlemen  It is with great emotion and joy that I address you. First of all, I would like to express my warmest and most sincere gratitude and thanks to His Excellency Mr. Francois HOLLANDE, President of the French Republic for the honor he has given me by appointing me to this high honorary distinction of Officer of the National Order of Merit. I confess that the surprise was total when I received the letter from Ambassador de France announcing this excellent news. I felt a great emotion because I was returning to work that day after a few days of hospitalization in Reunion and, when the Vice-Governor handed me all the pending files, I expected everything but not to receive the announcement of such a distinction. Mr Ambassador, it is with great pleasure, great joy and immense pride that I have just received from your hands these insignia of Officer of the National Order of Merit, on behalf of H.E. Francois HOLLANDE, President of the French Republic. I appreciate the significance of this prestigious distinction. This is an intense moment for me and I am convinced that this ceremony is not an end, an end in itself, or the crowning achievement of a career. On the contrary, allow me to consider this distinction as a new beginning, which only increases my motivation, my enthusiasm to serve my country and to further promote cooperation between France and the Comoros. I would like to thank you, Mr Ambassador, yourself and especially you, who have offered me to benefit from this high distinction and to tell you that I am very honored, moved, happy and proud to be among those whom the French Republic has distinguished. I receive this distinction with great gravity but also with great modesty. Indeed, this honour does not belong to me alone. Through me, it is the Central Bank, its directors, its staff and its partners, that the President of the French Republic wanted to distinguish. We are all grateful. Mr. Ambassador, the words you have just spoken about me touch me very sincerely and go straight to my heart. I thank you and your wife, Mrs. Rabia Bekkar-LACOSTE, for having done me the honor of organizing in your residence this beautiful and moving ceremony. I will no doubt remember for a very long time the pleasure you gave me by inviting on this occasion the political and diplomatic authorities, the heads of banks and companies, friends, relatives, friends of my father, my children and my dear wife. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, So many of you have kindly honoured this ceremony with your presence. Thank you for your presence, which honours me and also honours the Central Bank. I would also like to thank the France for having given me this honour, because this is indeed the France, a country for which I have great sincere and genuine esteem, the country that welcomed me for several years, the country that opened the doors of its universities to me and allowed me to study at a high quality. This country that opened the door to its great institution, the BDF, where I did my 1st internship, which was for me a springboard to enter the Central Bank and serve my country at a high level. For me, France and the Comoros are two totally linked countries. Today, France carries many dreams and hopes, especially for young students who aspire to access its universities, schools, to become doctors, lawyers, engineers, economists, bankers, .... I had this dream and I realized it thanks to the cooperation between France and the Comoros. Allow me to salute the efforts made in recent years by you, Mr Ambassador, in giving many students the chance to realize their dream, this dream of becoming better trained men and women, capable of meeting the great challenges of tomorrow. Allow me also to salute the actions developed by your wife with the University of the Comoros and her commitment to the international influence of this young university. I taught courses on currency and banking for three years and I appreciate the scope of its assistance. Distinguished guests, I would like to share this honor with many people: First of all, I have a grateful thought for my parents and grandparents who raised me in the best Comorian traditions, based on respect, the value of work, perseverance and honesty. I have a very deep thought for my grandmother who was affectionately called "Mche tourou", she was a beautiful and tireless woman. She has remained my source of inspiration and my reference. Honourable guests, ladies and gentlemen, A decoration symbolizes a particular moment in a career, probably related to a result. For me, it is 17 years in the service of my country and the Central Bank, as a senior manager, department director, vice-governor and then governor. I thank all those who have given me this opportunity to serve my country at this high level. First of all, HE former President Azali Assoumani, who was the 1st to trust me to occupy and for the 1st time in the history of the BCC, the position of 1st Comorian Vice-Governor. Seven years later, HE President IKILILOU DHOININE has enhanced this confidence by appointing me to the post of Governor, I renew all my gratitude. A big thank you also to Vice-President Mohamed Ali Soilihi, who associates me with his great international experience, through the negotiations in which I have the chance to participate in his committees; Our country derives great success and satisfaction from it. Distinguished guests, In 2005, appointed Vice-Governor, I quickly measured the road ahead, I understood that there were many things to do, that it was necessary to breathe momentum, dare to propose change, convince, reassure; Because in a sometimes difficult environment, change is not a source of instability, it can, on the contrary, create stability. When I look at the path we have travelled together and in such a short time, political authorities, Executive Directors and staff of the Bank, development partners, I see that we have taken a giant step forward in many areas: monetary policy, banking supervision, reform of the legal and regulatory framework for the exercise of banking activity, the fight against money laundering, the opening of the banking sector, the regulation and security of means of payment. The statutes of the BCC have been reformed, its expertise and level of intervention have been strengthened, its international openness has been intensified, its organization and its governance and control system have been reformed. The Central Bank is thus able to respond to the challenges of major projects underway for the consolidation of the banking sector. This reinforces our conviction that our country is on the path to its development. I can only salute those who have contributed and given more content to this journey. Ladies and gentlemen As you know, the world and the world economy today evolve within the framework of large ensembles. The Comoros belongs to a group that has already existed for more than 50 years, a set that has proved its worth, which has made it possible to ensure the stability of our currency. This group is the Franc Zone, which today constitutes an asset that provides member countries with monetary stability and banking solidity, through discipline and solidarity. This group is also evolving with subsets, towards banking unions, towards macroeconomic convergence, towards regional integrations and towards major reforms. In this trajectory, our country is part of it, cooperates, develops real partnerships. Last December, at the invitation of Mr Pierre Moscovici, French Minister of Economy and Finance, the Vice-President in charge of Finance and I We even participated in the Bercy conference whose theme was "economic partnership and development" and the objective of identifying the themes of economic cooperation between France and Africa in the economic agenda of the Elysee summit in which HE President IKILILOU DHOININE took part. Key topics for cooperation were discussed, in particular:  Human and intellectual exchanges,  Developing financing instruments for growth economic,  The development of different economic flows, including issues related to the fluidity of diaspora transfers, business financing, the digital economy,  legal integration and investment security. I am convinced that our country will jump on the bandwagon of cooperation around these major development issues. Let me conclude with a few thanks. I thank my 2nd mother who is here, Mrs. Mariam Mbae, my family who lives in France, my nephews and nieces who are here, my sisters and brothers-in-law. Finally, I would like to thank my wife, Djaidata, an exceptional, tenacious woman, who accepts my long working days, my absences for external missions, understanding the constraints related to my heavy responsibility. I thank her, she who lent me a hand, supported me with lucidity, for her love and her unwavering support for 20 years to my ctes. She is the privileged witness of my professional career and the different stages I have taken. She has a lot to do with this distinction and I share it with her. I thank my children, for the joy they bring me, they are also the source of my motivation, I learn a lot with them, they are today my pride and my future. Thank you.

Title: New Year I Greetings from the Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros.
text: New Year I New Year's greetings from the Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros. I would like to take this opportunity to send you, on behalf of all the staff of the Central Bank, my sincere wishes for a happy new year 2023. I hope that this The new year will be a source of health, happiness, happiness and happiness for all of us. success and success in our respective companies. I hope that this year 2023 will be the year of recovery for our economy, which has been severely impacted by the global health crisis and the war in Ukraine. For several years, the Central Bank has initiated several reforms to support the development of the banking sector. In 2023, it will continue this dynamic to meet the country's economic development objectives and also the objectives of modernizing the Central Bank of the Comoros. The year 2023 will be a year of implementation of new monetary policy instruments, including the creation of a securities market and also a year of financial inclusion and an increase in the rate of banking access, currently estimated at only 24%. Among the major projects selected, some of which have already been initiated within the BCC, we note: o The revision of certain regulatory texts, in particular the statutes of the BCC and its internal regulations o The search for sustainable solutions to financial institutions in difficulty o Strengthening the legislative and regulatory framework for the resolution of banking crises o Addressing non-performing loans in the banking system o The modernisation of the national payment system in order to allow, in particular, increasing financial inclusion; For the first time in the history of the BCC, we will: o Modernise our monetary policy through the creation of an interbank market and a Government securities market o Implement new instruments for mobilizing savings and granting credits: Islamic Finance, Diaspora Finance, Leasing o Implement an Overall Effective Rate and a usury rate that will contribute to the Lower interest rates o Set up a Guarantee Fund and encourage the creation of a Bank investments as a means of granting medium and long-term credit, o And finally, we are going to strengthen the national system for the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism. Internally, the Central Bank is modernising and will continue its work by: o Strengthening transparency through the implementation of an adapted communication plan by referring to the best practices of other Central Banks o The operationalization of the Banking Training Center and the establishment of a Documentation Center o The implementation of electronic archiving - The realization of the rehabilitation work of the Anjouan branch to respond to the increase in economic activities of this island. o The acquisition of new automatic banknote sorting machines I would like to take this opportunity to reiterate my sincere thanks to all our partners who provide their financial and technical support to the BCC in the implementation of its various projects, in particular the Banque de France, the Monnaie de Paris, the AFD, the IMF, the World Bank, the IEDOM, the BCEAO, the BEAC, the Bank al Maghrib. Mwaha Mwema, Dr Younoussa IMANI Governor of the Central Bank of the Comoros
